_doc: N-160: a treeIdx < 2^63 (lo) sibling to the F-034 witness's treeIdx >= 2^63 (hi) SLH-DSA-SHA2-256f vector, so a permanent test exercises BOTH sides of the h-h'>=64 tree-address boundary (F-034 fixed the wide arm but the witness that pinned the golden only exercised the hi side). Signed by the SAME third-party implementation and the SAME keypair as conformance/witnesses/real-crypto/post-quantum-slhdsa-256f.json: PyPI slh-dsa 0.2.5, Sha2_1Parameter(25, 32, 68, 17, 4, 9, 35, 4, 49) (that library's FIPS 205 SHA-256-only Sec 11.2.1 instantiation at the 256f dimensions -- the repo's on-chain variant, since Bitcoin Script has no OP_SHA512, issue #137). sk_seed/sk_prf/pk_seed = SHA-256('runar F-034 sk_seed' / 'runar F-034 sk_prf' / 'runar F-034 pk_seed'); pk_root computed the same way slhdsa.lowlevel.slhdsa.keygen does (XMSS(par).node(sk_seed, 0, par.h_m, pk_seed, Address(par.d-1, 0))), which reproduces the exact F-034 witness pubkey byte for byte. Internal (pre-hash-free) sign, deterministic: SecretKey.sign(msg, randomize=False) -> opt_rand = pk_seed. msg = UTF-8 'runar N-160 SLH-DSA-SHA2-256f lo witness 1' (chosen by trying successive suffixes against the fixed keypair until Hmsg produced a tree index < 2^63; this is message selection, not key or seed manipulation). No compiler or repo signer (packages/runar-testing/src/crypto/slh-dsa.ts) was used to produce this signature; slh-dsa.ts's own slhVerifyVerbose is used only to CROSS-CHECK the pinned treeIdx below, never to sign.
